demo.title: Demo
demo.components.heading: Selector and any-picker
demo.components.intro: Demonstrates the Selector dialog (T-96), the any-picker and the icon-picker. Owner has a Browse button that opens the Selector: it lists the active users of your tenant whose role is equal to or lower than yours, with search and paging, and choosing a row fills the field. Reviewer is the same widget with a small icon-only Browse button (x-seam-browse) and a marker-style match highlight (x-seam-highlight); type a few letters to see both. Code is a plain field with an explicit placeholder (x-seam-placeholder). Icon searches the Material Icons by name; its Browse button opens a scrollable grid of every icon (the grid and the dropdown are never open together), and the chosen icon stays visible beside the box. Submit to see the values the server receives.
demo.repeatable.heading: Repeatable rows with no fields
demo.repeatable.intro: Answer to the Work Orders developers' report: repeatable rows appeared with only the remove button. A repeatable takes its row fields only from a field declared "type": "array" with "items" and "properties". The reported schema used "type": "object" with a non-standard "line_items" key, and "type": "string" with "items", so no row fields were found. The add button now also finds its own container, so each block adds its own lines.
demo.repeatable.after: Corrected (rendered by the real form engine)
demo.echo.title: Posted values
demo.echo.intro: This is what the server received (the CSRF token is omitted). Nothing was saved.
demo.repeatable.naming: Rows that hold nested rows or a user picker use indexed field names, for example blocks[0][lines][1][name], and the server rebuilds the structure: submit the form and look at the structured value. A repeatable without nesting keeps the flat names (workflow_states_name[]). A row whose first field is empty is dropped. Inside repeatable rows use any-picker, not asset-picker.
demo.echo.structured: Structured value rebuilt by the server
demo.saved.heading: Saved demo records
demo.saved.note: Stored only in the demo_templates entity of your tenant, marked as demo data. No other module reads or writes it, and the buttons below delete only those records.
demo.save.name_required: Enter a template name before saving.
demo.repeatable.rows: Each cell names itself with a placeholder: the field's title, or its x-seam-placeholder (as in Block name and Tag). Blocks uses x-seam-layout: form, so each block is a card with labelled fields; Workflow keeps the default single-line rows. Nested Lines sit indented under a coloured rule with their own heading and tint. The Icon and Responsible pickers work inside rows, including rows you add. Add and remove use the same icon buttons as the rest of the UI.
demo.kitchen_rows.heading: Kitchen sink: widgets inside repeatable rows
demo.kitchen_rows.intro: A repeatable whose rows hold the widgets that need a script: masked text and phone, a barcode with live preview, a GPS map, a signature pad, an asset picker and an icon picker. Add rows and use every control: each new row works like the first.
demo.kitchen_rows.notes: These widgets are plain markup that one shared script (SeamWidgets) initialises, in the first rows and in the rows you add. Rows use indexed field names, as pickers always did. Submit to see the structure the server rebuilds, with the signature as a data URL.
demo.kitchen_inputs.heading: Kitchen sink: inputs
demo.kitchen_inputs.intro: Every text-like, numeric and date widget of the form engine in one form: masked text and phone, email, URL, password, date, date and time, time, number and decimal with units, long text, colour, checkbox and switch.
demo.kitchen_inputs.notes: Each field's help text names the schema property it demonstrates. Submit to see the exact strings the server receives: the unit is not part of a value, and the server never fills in the password field. Repeatables and buttons have their own tabs.
demo.kitchen_choices.heading: Kitchen sink: choices and pickers
demo.kitchen_choices.intro: Selects of every kind (static, searchable, grouped, with icons, from a foreign key), the multiple-choice group, the asset and record pickers, the icon picker and conditional visibility.
demo.kitchen_choices.notes: Try Severity (High or Critical) and Shutdown reason (Other) to see fields appear and disappear. Brand and the pickers read your tenant's data, so they are empty on a fresh instance. Submit to see what is posted.
demo.kitchen_field.heading: Kitchen sink: location, barcodes and signature
demo.kitchen_field.intro: The widgets that draw something: a map with a draggable marker (GPS), live barcodes in three symbologies, a signature pad and the photo gallery.
demo.kitchen_field.notes: The map tiles come from OpenStreetMap, so they need internet access. Depot location, EAN-13, EAN-8 and UPC-A open with stored values. Photos needs a saved record, so here it only shows its message. Submit to see the posted coordinates and the signature as a data URL.
demo.schema.heading: Schema
demo.layouts.heading: Row and form layouts
demo.layouts.intro: A repeatable lays its rows out in one of two ways, set with x-seam-layout. Row (the default) puts every cell of a line on one line, like the Document Links of the Assets form: Expense lines and Checklist use it. Form turns each row into a card with labelled cells in a responsive grid: Contacts uses it.
demo.layouts.notes: Phases shows both together: each phase is a form-layout card and its Tasks, nested inside, keep one-line rows. Add and remove rows at both levels, then submit to see the structure the server rebuilds from the indexed field names.
demo.buttons.heading: Add and remove buttons
demo.buttons.intro: The add and remove buttons of a repeatable can be changed from the schema: x-seam-add-label, x-seam-add-icon and x-seam-add-style (outline, filled, link or icon) for the add button; x-seam-remove-icon and x-seam-remove-label for the remove button. Icon names are Material Icons names.
demo.buttons.notes: Each repeatable below changes a different set: Tags uses a link-style add button, Steps a filled one and a labelled remove button, Attachments an icon-only add button (its label is the tooltip), Approvers a custom label and icon on the default outlined button. Rows you add keep the custom remove button.
demo.colors.heading: Accent colours
demo.colors.intro: x-seam-accent colours a repeatable's rows, add button and nested rule; x-seam-remove-color colours the remove buttons. A colour is a name (indigo, emerald, amber, rose, sky, violet, teal or slate) or a #rrggbb value; anything else is ignored and the theme colours stay. Both work in light and dark mode.
demo.colors.notes: Baseline has no accent, for comparison. Risks and Notes show a named accent with a matching or contrasting remove colour, Milestones combines an accent with a filled add button, and Custom hex colour uses #7c3aed with nested Lines that have an accent of their own.
demo.selectors.heading: Selectors over several entities
demo.selectors.intro: The any-picker works over any entity registered on the server. Each field below searches as you type, and the ones with x-seam-selector also have a Browse button that opens the Selector dialog: Asset (name, tag, status, criticality), Cost center, Location, Custodian and Owner (users). Spare location has no Browse button, only live search.
demo.selectors.notes: Assignments puts three different pickers in the same repeatable row, each with its own Selector, and rows you add get working pickers too. The records come from your tenant's data (for example the seeded assets, cost centers, locations and custodians). Submit to see the ids the server receives.
demo.reorder.heading: Reordering rows and searchable selects
demo.reorder.intro: Set x-seam-reorder on a repeatable to give every row a drag handle. Drag the grip, or focus it and use the Arrow keys (Home and End jump to the ends). Steps uses flat field names, so the browser posts the rows in the new order; Checklist and Stages use indexed names, where each row also posts its position. Without x-seam-reorder, as in Fixed list, rows keep their place.
demo.reorder.notes: Every select on this page is a searchable combobox: Category has enough options to show a search box, Priority is short and shows none. Add rows, move them around and submit to see the order the server receives.

accounting.formula.title: Formulas
accounting.formula.intro: A rule turns a reference amount into a new one. Each rule takes its figure from a simple percentage, a fixed amount, or the result of OQL queries, and either sets the running amount, adds a surcharge to it or subtracts a discount from it. Rules run in order, top to bottom.
accounting.formula.situation.commission_: What an AE earns on a collected item. The running amount starts at zero; a percentage "set" is taken of what the customer paid. With no enabled rule here, the rates from the settings apply.
accounting.formula.situation.price_help: The price of an item in a market. The running amount starts at the base (master list) price; a discount or surcharge changes it.
accounting.formula.delete_confirm: Delete the rule “%s”? Commission lines already booked keep their amounts.

accounting.formula.conditions_help: Leave a field empty for any. Every field that is filled in must match.
accounting.formula.field.name: Name
accounting.formula.field.effect_help: Set replaces the running amount (a percentage is then taken of the reference amount). Surcharge adds to it and discount subtracts from it (a percentage is then taken of the running amount). The amount never goes below zero.
accounting.formula.field.percent_help: For example 12.5 means 12.5 percent. Up to two decimals.
accounting.formula.field.amount_help: A fixed amount in USD, for example 25.00.
accounting.formula.field.queries_help: Write one or more SELECT queries and separate them with a line holding only a semicolon (;). The last query must return a single value: the amount in USD cents. Earlier queries are for working things out: each result is available to the next as :prev and, by position, as :q1, :q2…
accounting.formula.field.queries_example: Example: SELECT SUM(amount) AS v FROM adm_item WHERE tenant_id = :tenant_id AND period = :period — the total billed to that tenant in that period. Only reading is allowed, on the business tables (adm_item, adm_tenant, adm_commission, adm_settlement, adm_close, adm_entry, adm_movement, adm_account, adm_line_claim).

demo.query_picker.heading: Query picker: choose a record from an OQL query
demo.query_picker.intro: Each field below lists the rows of its own OQL query, with typed columns: text, numbers, money, dates and badges. Type at least two characters to search. The query stays on the server: the page carries only a sealed reference to it.
demo.query_picker.notes: Asset uses the table layout, a Browse button and a detail line; Model uses the rows layout and resolves the brand with a lookup instead of a JOIN; Asset by type runs one JOIN because the search also looks at the type's name; Lines puts the picker inside repeatable rows. The records come from your tenant, and submitting checks that each value is a row its query returns.

designer.prop.x-seam-placeholder.help: Text shown in an empty control; for a select, the text of its empty option.
designer.prop.x-seam-query.title: Query
designer.prop.x-seam-query.help: One read-only OQL SELECT with named columns, every LIKE in its own parentheses, an ORDER BY and no TOP. Parameters: :q, :q_raw, :tenant_id, :user_id.
designer.prop.x-seam-relation.title: Relation
designer.prop.x-seam-relation.help: The kind of link of the asset graph to follow.
designer.prop.x-seam-remove-color.title: Remove button colour
designer.prop.x-seam-remove-icon.title: Remove button icon
designer.prop.x-seam-remove-label.title: Remove button text
designer.prop.x-seam-remove-label.help: Text beside the remove icon of each row.
designer.prop.x-seam-reorder.title: Reorderable
designer.prop.x-seam-reorder.help: Let the rows be dragged into a new order.
designer.prop.x-seam-rows.title: Rows
designer.prop.x-seam-rows.help: The height of the text area, in lines.
designer.prop.x-seam-search-fields.title: Search fields
designer.prop.x-seam-search-fields.help: The fields the search looks in, one per line.
designer.prop.x-seam-selector.title: Selector
designer.prop.x-seam-selector.help: The Selector source to browse, for example users; adds a Browse button. On a query-picker, write query to browse the field's own query.
designer.prop.x-seam-source.title: Source
designer.prop.x-seam-source.help: Where the options come from, for example entity:users.
designer.prop.x-seam-unit.title: Unit
designer.prop.x-seam-unit.help: A unit shown after the control, for example kg. Display only.
designer.prop.x-seam-value-field.title: Value column
designer.prop.x-seam-value-field.help: The result column stored as the field's value; id when empty.
designer.prop.x-seam-visible-when.title: Visible when
designer.prop.x-seam-visible-when.help: A condition on other fields, as JSON, under which the field is shown.

developer.translations.state.untranslate: Same as the reference text: not translated
developer.translations.state.missing: No text: the reference text is shown
developer.forms.label_keys_guess: The form's page has not been opened since the server started, so these keys follow the naming convention. Open the page once to see the ones it asks for.
developer.layers.refused: Set aside because they could not be read or shown; what was in use for each form stays, and the other files are loaded:
developer.try.title: Try %s

developer.try.empty: Submit the form to see what the server receives.
developer.try.errors: Some fields were not accepted; they are marked in the form.
developer.try.sources: These lists are filled by the form's own page and may be empty here: %s
developer.try.none: Nothing is in use for this form yet: save a definition first.
developer.layers.refused_locales: Set aside because they could not be read; the texts each language had before stay in use, and the other files are loaded:
developer.flag.module_demo.title: Demo module
developer.flag.module_demo.desc: Switch the Demo module on for this tenant without a restart. It is off at startup.
developer.flag.module_work_orders.title: Work Orders module
developer.flag.module_work_orders.desc: Switch the Work Orders module on for this tenant without a restart. It is off at startup.
developer.flag.module_issues.title: Issues module
developer.flag.module_issues.desc: Switch the Issues module on for this tenant without a restart. It is off at startup.
developer.startup.settings_note: Set at startup, in the configuration file or the environment. They are not switches.
developer.setting.poll: How often an override directory is loaded while its hot-load switch is on.
developer.setting.history: How often an override directory is looked at for the history of changes made in the files.
developer.setting.sync: How often this instance checks what another instance changed.
developer.setting.global_tenant: The tenant whose developers may edit overrides that apply to every tenant.
developer.setting.source_dir: The source checkout scanned for texts no code refers to.
developer.setting.on_load: only when the directory is loaded
developer.scope.global.hint: Saved in the database for every tenant. A tenant's own override, and a file override, win over it.
developer.scope.global.shadowed: This tenant's own override, or one in the files, outranks this one here; other tenants see it.
developer.try.record_hint: Optional: an ID. That record is left out of the lists, as on a page that edits it.
developer.setting.module_audience: Who a module switched on from the panel is on for: the tenant's developers, or every user of the tenant.
developer.setting.watch: How the override directories are followed for the history: the system's change events, or polling.
developer.setting.custom_pages: Whether a form created with the tools gets a page of its own, with its submissions kept.
developer.setting.preferences: Where a developer's last choices are kept: with the account, or in the browser only.
developer.translations.source.prefix: Built at run time from "%s", which is written in:
developer.translations.source.convention: Built by the form engine's naming convention; no file spells it out.%s
developer.translations.source.parts: Probably assembled from parts: each of its parts is in the source, the whole key is not.%s
developer.translations.source.none: Nothing in the source refers to it.%s
developer.custom.not_saved: It could not be saved. Try again.
developer.custom.submissions: Its page and what it has received

developer.designer.layout.label: Label
developer.designer.layout.join: Put beside the section before it
developer.designer.layout.split: Give it a row of its own
developer.designer.layout.extras_note: Each is a JSON list of objects, as the form engine reads them. Empty removes them.
developer.designer.layout.hint: Drag a field onto a section, or onto another field to go before it. Everything a drag does can also be done with the controls.
developer.designer.layout.duplicate_tab: Duplicate tab, with copies of its fields
developer.designer.layout.duplicate_sect: Duplicate section, with copies of its fields
